name: Teaching

levels.note: 12th pass + teaching diploma. CTET Paper 1 (Classes 1–5). Age 18–35.
Graduation in relevant subject + B.Ed. CTET Paper 2 (Classes 6–8) or State TET.
Master's degree. UGC-NET or Ph.D for Assistant Professor. Age 21–40.

stages.name: Written Exam
stages.tests: CTET: 150 Qs, 150 min. Child Pedagogy, Subject, Language I & II, EVS/Maths.
stages.note: Qualifying. 60% to pass. Valid for lifetime (from 2021).

stages.name: Interview / Demo
stages.tests: Teaching demo (10–15 min) + personal interview. Subject knowledge + pedagogy.
stages.note: KVS/NVS have interview. State TET recruitments may skip interview (merit-based).

stages.name: Document Verification
stages.tests: Degree, B.Ed, TET certificate, caste, domicile, NOC.
stages.note: B.Ed must be from NCTE-recognised institution. Verify before applying.

stages.name: Medical & Joining
stages.tests: Basic medical fitness. Joining in allotted school/region.
stages.note: KVS/NVS have transferable posts. State boards: home state preference.

reality: CTET is qualifying only — it doesn't get you a job. You need a recruitment exam (KVS, NVS, state boards) separately.
KVS and NVS are central; state boards are state-specific. Apply to both for more chances.
B.Ed is mandatory for TGT/PGT. Without B.Ed, only PRT (primary) posts are open.
State TET (like UPTET, HTET) is separate from CTET. Some states accept CTET; many require state TET.
Teaching jobs have high competition. KVS PGT attracts 50,000+ applicants for 1000 posts.
Salary: KVS PGT ~₹47,600 (Level 8) + DA + HRA. State varies. Private schools pay less.

faq.q: What is CTET and is it mandatory?
faq.a: Central Teacher Eligibility Test — qualifying exam for teaching Classes 1–8 in central schools (KVS, NVS, Army schools). Mandatory for central recruitment. State schools may require state TET instead.

faq.q: Can a B.Tech graduate become a teacher?
faq.a: Yes. B.Tech + B.Ed makes you eligible for TGT (Maths/Science) in KVS, NVS, and state boards. Some states allow B.Tech without B.Ed for specific subjects.

faq.q: What is the difference between KVS and NVS?
faq.a: KVS = Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan (urban, central government employees' children). NVS = Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti (rural, free residential schools). Both central, similar pay, different locations.

faq.q: How many vacancies are there in teaching?
faq.a: KVS recruits 5,000–10,000+ annually. NVS recruits 2,000–3,000. State boards vary widely (UP TGT: 10,000+). Total government teaching vacancies exceed 1 lakh per year.

faq.q: What is the age limit for teaching jobs?
faq.a: KVS: 18–35 years (PRT), 21–35 (TGT/PGT). NVS: similar. State boards: varies (often 21–40). Age relaxations for SC/ST/OBC/PwD.

faq.q: Where do I find official teaching notifications?
faq.a: kvs.gov.in (KVS), navodaya.gov.in (NVS), cbse.gov.in (CTET), and state education boards. SarkariJobs+ links the official notification on every listing.
